correctness.rationale: For every x_*>0, B,p,alpha,kappa>0, q>=0 and Delta=p*kappa-alpha*q>0, the model Jacobian has negative trace and positive determinant at every r>0, hence its stationary Gaussian covariance is unique. Exact symbolic solution of the three independent Lyapunov equations yields s,t,u; s>0 and the Schur complement yields the displayed V(r). Setting rho=q/B and eta=alpha*q/(kappa*p) reduces V-1 to a scalar rational function. Its derivative numerator factors as (1-rho)^2(1-eta)-(z+rho)^2, which proves every monotone and unimodal regime without finite sampling. Reference equilibrium root is bracketed by exact rational polynomial signs; the standalone symbolic and high-precision checker reproduces r_star and Vmax. No assertion extends the stationary Gaussian result to the full extinction-prone jump process.

The broader slow-scale LNA and metabolic feedback-noise studies use general techniques or a distinct model. The new claim is a precise model-specific quantitative classification; standard Gaussian conditioning, Lyapunov analysis, and optimization are not claimed novel. Prior coverage may exist as an unstated corollary or generalized formula; accessible primary text and actual research searches were compared and do not decisively cover the final exact statement.

value.rationale: The motivating primary research explicitly studies conditional stationary signal-noise ratios as turnover changes and gives three illustrative rates; those points cannot establish whether an interior maximum is unique or determine its optimal tuning. The theorem classifies all stable positive equilibria into above- or below-Poisson conditional-noise regimes and gives a sharp necessary/sufficient peak criterion and exact maximizing timescale. The model-specific signal-noise resonance is a natural quantitative invariant for assessing turnover experiments and checking Gaussian approximations; it is more than a gratuitous parameter substitution or tabular recomputation. Its utility and limitations are explicit; nothing is claimed about extinction optimization or finite-N stationary laws.
